This hospital may not be a "7-star" facility when judged purely on luxury or infrastructure, but it is unquestionably 7-star when it comes to patient care, professionalism, and service.

My father was admitted after battling a serious infection for several days and required immediate medical attention. From the moment he arrived, the hospital team acted quickly and thoroughly. The doctors conducted a comprehensive diagnosis, identified the bacteria causing the infection, and started the right treatment without delay.

What impressed our family most was the level of care shown by everyone involved. The doctors, nurses, support staff, and even the cleaning team treated my father with kindness, respect, and genuine concern. Beyond treating the infection, the team focused on helping him regain his strength and recover comfortably.

No stone was left unturned during his stay. Every necessary test was completed, his condition was closely monitored, and we were kept informed throughout the process. Thanks to the excellent care he received, my father made a remarkable recovery and was discharged after just four days.

We are deeply grateful to the entire team for their dedication, compassion, and professionalism. While buildings and facilities are important, it is the people who make a hospital exceptional, and this hospital truly excels where it matters most.

featured_reviews.name: Prakhar Gupta
featured_reviews.review_text:
Absolutely shameful and horrifying experience.

I called the hospital in the middle of the night asking for an ambulance for my father during a medical emergency. Instead of helping, they kept me on hold and slowly kept reciting a phone number to call myself while I was trying to manage my father’s condition.

The hospital was barely 7 minutes away, yet the ambulance took around 30 minutes to arrive at 2 AM. Those minutes matter in an emergency.

And the nightmare did not end there.

After reaching the hospital, there was no stretcher ready, no emergency staff attending immediately, and we literally had to shout for help while bringing in a critical patient.

Most shocking of all, the ambulance did not even have a proper oxygen mask available.

No family should ever have to go through this level of negligence during a life-and-death emergency. A hospital that advertises emergency care should at the very least have a functioning emergency response system, trained staff ready to act, and properly equipped ambulances.

I would strongly urge people to think twice before depending on this hospital in a real emergency situation.

Yesterday (22 december 2025) I had an appointment with Dr. Amit Mishra at 8pm.
I reached Satya hospital at 7.30ish since I came directly after work. So I was aware that I would have to wait until 8pm at least.
At first, I waited until 8.20pm (which is already a little late for my 8pm appointment) and asked the receptionist how long would it take? She said that there was another patient before me who still had to go and then it would be my turn.
I waited and waited and then at 9.15pm she tells me that I could visit now!!! When I go upstairs I see 5 other people standing there.. and confirm from the nurse if they're waiting in line. She says yes there are 3 or 4 patients to be attended to before my turn.
I wonder how long more it would have taken because I informed the receptionist to cancel my appointment and walked out of the hospital!
The whole idea of taking appointments is so that people are aware of the time they have to be there at. It's very disrespectful to keep people waiting without giving any valid reason. I would have understood if there was any emergency that was being attended to but again it should be communicated properly. Please make sure to have a better organization system or don't take too many patients if you can't handle it time wise.. Or just cancel the whole appointment format and keep it walk in! I'm really very disappointed and frustrated with my first time experience here to have waited for almost 1 hour 15 mins (only including time since appointment time schedule)

The campus itself is beautiful and well maintained. Online appointment booking is smooth, while offline booking starts at 7:30 am and doctors typically begin consultations from around 8:30 am.

The private consultation experience (ENT, in my case) was genuinely good. The doctor gave adequate time, listened patiently, and the interaction felt reassuring and professional. However, this comes at a cost, as the visit including diagnostics ended up in the range of ₹3,000–4,000.

The general OPD experience was very bad. The charges are in the range of ₹400-700.

Earlier I had positive experiences with  Gastroenterology and Surgery. I was very much impressed with the surgeon, but his opinion was outrightly dismissed by 3 other senior surgeons and physicians. I realised he kept focussing on a know problem which wasn't connected to my pain.  Gastroenterologist doesn't do any physical examination to understand the location of pain or confirm hemorrhoids. Seems, he only checks you during pricey colonoscopy and endoscopy procedures.

My experience with General Medicine and Urology OPD was disappointing. In these departments, the main doctor and an assistant doctor sit at the same small table and consult two different patients simultaneously.

In General Medicine OPD, there were up to four patients along with their attendants inside the same room at once—one with the main doctor, one with the assistant, one waiting behind the doctor, and another at the entrance being triaged for blood pressure and weight. That easily translates to 8–10 people in a single consultation room. There is no space for discussion, questions, nuance, or privacy. The doctor barely had time for eye contact, let alone a detailed conversation or examination.

In the Urology OPD, I could speak to the actual doctor only after the assistant doctor felt I was not convinced. While I do not question the competence of junior doctors, as a patient it feels unfair when you do not get adequate time with the consultant you booked.

I guess this is the truth of INR 400-700 consultations. I sincerely hope the PRO and hospital administration take note of these inconsistencies, especially given Holy Spirit’s reputation as an esteemed institution.
